macro.summary: July US CPI was benign enough to reduce immediate Fed-hike pressure, supporting growth and automation multiples at the margin, but oil remains elevated and the US 10-year yield remains high. Power scarcity, grid equipment, gas/nuclear generation and physical infrastructure therefore remain higher-conviction than long-duration speculative technology.
macro.portfolioRead: Keep a barbell between quality physical-infrastructure names and selected growth/robotics exposures with proven deployment economics. Avoid broad theme-chasing in pre-commercial humanoids.

categoryRanking.reason: AI/data-centre load growth, grid bottlenecks and high power prices remain structural. Prefer GEV, PWR, ETN and selective generation exposure.
Elevated Brent and Hormuz risk support upstream and refining cash flows, while gas infrastructure also benefits from power demand.
Physical AI adoption is real but uneven. Warehouse automation, machine vision and cobots clear the ROI bar before humanoids.
Existing nuclear generation and fuel infrastructure retain scarcity value, but development-stage reactor equities remain valuation-sensitive.
AI infrastructure earnings remain strong, but rates and oil-driven inflation make high-multiple pure plays more fragile than grid and power suppliers.
Copper remains the cleaner cross-theme exposure through grid, motors, cables and robotics electrification.

existingIdeaChanges.reason: Elevated crude and geopolitical supply risk improve near-term upstream cash-flow conditions while integrated assets provide downside resilience.
CNOOC offers higher direct crude beta than integrated Chinese peers and remains a cleaner expression of sustained $80+ oil.
Product-market tightness and crack-spread strength improve the refining setup beyond a simple crude-price call.
Same product-tightness thesis as MPC, with cleaner refining beta but greater cyclicality.
AI infrastructure demand remains strong, but high theme dependency and valuation sensitivity argue against upgrading after the recent earnings-led sector rally.
Power scarcity, generation backlog and grid bottlenecks remain among the strongest cross-theme exposures in the Stack.
RM1.16bn orders in hand and TNB-linked cable demand provide strong Malaysian grid visibility through 2027.
Delivered and secured data-centre capacity continues to rise, but the stock remains more theme-sensitive than TNB and cable/grid names.
Warehouse automation is the first robotics adoption wave. Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 23% YoY to $676m, adjusted EBITDA reached $78m and systems in deployment rose to 70.
Geekplus provides direct listed AMR exposure with 2025 revenue and orders both up roughly 32% and adjusted profitability turning positive.
Machine vision is form-factor agnostic robotics infrastructure and can benefit across industrial arms, AMRs, cobots and humanoids.
Universal Robots and MiR create a useful robotics crossover alongside AI semiconductor test exposure.
Industrial humanoids are a plausible third-wave deployment category, but repeat commercial orders and unit economics are not yet sufficiently de-risked.

newOpportunities.name: Talen Energy
newOpportunities.thesis: Merchant and contracted generation exposure spanning nuclear and dispatchable gas, with direct large-load/data-centre relevance in PJM.
newOpportunities.catalysts: 10,180 MW cleared in PJM's 2028/29 capacity auction, roughly $1.208bn of associated capacity revenue, AWS/data-centre contracting and fleet expansion.
newOpportunities.risks: Merchant-power volatility, leverage, acquisition integration and regulatory risk.
newOpportunities.differentiation: More direct power-price and capacity-market exposure than equipment suppliers such as GEV or ETN.

newOpportunities.name: Gamuda
newOpportunities.thesis: Large Malaysian engineering and construction platform with direct exposure to the second wave of hyperscale data-centre construction while retaining broader infrastructure diversification.
newOpportunities.catalysts: Springhill campus buildout, follow-on data-centre structures and broader public infrastructure awards.
newOpportunities.risks: Construction margins, project timing and data-centre capex concentration.
newOpportunities.differentiation: Broader and financially more diversified construction exposure than smaller pure-play electrical contractors.

newOpportunities.name: Pekat Group
newOpportunities.thesis: Malaysia grid/solar/electrical-services adjacency that can benefit from data-centre power demand and green-electricity procurement without being a direct server-hardware bet.
newOpportunities.catalysts: Grid upgrades, data-centre electrical demand and corporate renewable procurement.
newOpportunities.risks: Small-cap execution, project concentration and policy sensitivity.
newOpportunities.differentiation: Adds distributed electrical and renewable-system exposure not already captured by TNB, Southern Cable or MN Holdings.

roboticsAdoptionOrder.investmentRead: Highest current ROI and lowest autonomy burden. Prefer SYM, Geekplus, machine-vision and industrial-control suppliers.
Best bridge from conventional automation into Physical AI. TER is a diversified listed crossover.
Pilots can scale in constrained factories, but reliability, dexterity and total cost of ownership remain the gating variables. Keep UBTECH speculative.
Too early for core Power Stack capital; treat as optionality rather than base-case earnings.
